## Summary

Deferred design work from [#160856](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/160856) (ES|QL datafeeds part 1: feature flag, config model, API gates). Part 1 intentionally lands config + gates; the items below need product/API decisions and follow-up PRs (mostly after query validation / extractor work in parts 2–4).

## Follow-ups

- [ ] **Infer `source_time_field` and `grouping_interval` for simple queries** — For queries with a single datetime output column or an obvious `BUCKET(@timestamp, …)` alias, deduce `source_time_field` and `grouping_interval` when omitted; otherwise fail with a clear “cannot deduce, specify explicitly” error.
- [ ] **Revisit `grouping_interval` vs job `bucket_span`** — Today `grouping_interval` must equal `bucket_span`. Evaluate removing `grouping_interval` from the API or deriving it once query analysis exists.
- [ ] **Security / privilege checks for ES|QL datafeed sources** — `DatafeedManager.putDatafeed` checks privileges on `indices`; ES|QL datafeeds need equivalent checks once source indices/clusters are known from the query (part 2+).
- [ ] **Remove `esql_datafeeds` feature flag before GA** — Flag gates create/start/preview until the stack is ready; remove the flag and release-build gating when ES|QL datafeeds GA.
- [ ] **Truncation detection vs `esql.query.result_truncation_max_size`** (bead `elastic-workspace-g2sz.59`) — Chunk truncation is keyed to `EsqlDataExtractor.INJECTED_ROW_LIMIT` (10_000) while ES|QL may cap lower via cluster setting; decide whether to read the effective max for both inject and detection.
- [ ] **Size ES|QL chunk shrink from last complete timestamp in truncated rows** ([#164119](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/164119) review, bead `elastic-workspace-g2sz.78`) — `ChunkedDataExtractor` today halves `chunkSpan` and re-queries until a window fits under the injected row cap. Review alternative: from the time-ordered truncated rows (up to 10k), set the next chunk end to the last *complete* emitted timestamp (aligned down to `grouping_interval`) so one retried query can finish without remainder delegation or many shrink attempts. Follow-up after B2 shrink lands in #164119.
- [ ] **Typed missing-index signal for deferred PUT validation** (bead `elastic-workspace-g2sz.74`) — `isDeferredExistenceFailure` treats any 400 `Unknown index [` as “index not yet”, including missing LOOKUP JOIN targets; distinguish not-yet-created index from wrong lookup index / unauthorized (related: `g2sz.54`). Land together with the typed no-project mint probe signal (`elastic-workspace-u66g`).
- [ ] **Typed no-project-versus-missing-qualified-project signal for the mint access probe** (bead `elastic-workspace-u66g`, [#163852](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/163852)) — `validateAccessForMint` today tells “routing matched no project” from “qualified project does not exist” by matching `NoMatchingProjectException` message text. Add a typed signal (field or subclass) and drop the message match. How ES|QL surfaces an unmatched qualified project versus index resolution (unverified; may be the same `NoMatchingProjectException` or a 400 `Unknown index [`) is open.
- [ ] **Move ES|QL `rowCount` out of the shared `DataExtractor.Result`** ([#160857](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/160857#discussion_r4230653310) review) — `Result.rowCount` (with `ROW_COUNT_UNKNOWN` for DSL extractors) only exists so `ChunkedDataExtractor` (part 3) can detect truncated ES|QL chunks. Once the extractor foundation (parts 2–3) is merged, carry the row count in an ES|QL-specific result type and drop it from the shared record.
- [ ] **MUST FIX before production: replace hand-written ES|QL parsing with `EsqlParser`** ([#160857](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/160857) review) — `EsqlQueryClauseScanner`, `EsqlDatafeedQueryValidator` (leading command, source index expressions) and `EsqlDatafeedColumnValues.isDateColumnType` re-implement ES|QL syntax and are brittle. Known gaps: nested comments (`/* /* */ FROM t`), subqueries (`FROM (FROM remote:logs)`), FORK, settings, backtick-quoted time field (`` `@timestamp` ``). Needs a main-scope dependency from the ml plugin on x-pack esql (today test-only); use `DataType.isDate` for column types.

- [ ] **Delete stale ES|QL source-checkpoint copies during nightly maintenance** (bead `elastic-workspace-g2sz.76`) — Rollover leaves one `{jobId}_esql_source_checkpoint` per results-index generation. The load fallback in #161724 (same block on #150006) takes at most 100 unsorted ids hits and treats that page's max `source_end_ms` as the checkpoint. Nightly maintenance should delete older copies and keep the greatest `source_end_ms`, including when that copy is still only in an older index. Deleting every off-alias copy drops the watermark when the datafeed has not persisted since rollover.

- [ ] **Decide sub-bucket and interim-result behaviour for raw-row (no STATS) ES|QL datafeeds before GA** — Today all ES|QL datafeeds require `grouping_interval == bucket_span`, chunked extraction floors the window to that interval (A4), and frequency must be a multiple of `grouping_interval` with a snapped default (A7, #161725). That matches aggregation-style datafeeds, not DSL scroll (sub-bucket frequency, interim results). Options: keep and document, or scope alignment and frequency rules to aggregating queries only (needs query scanner; touches A4/B4). Bead `elastic-workspace-g2sz.77`; related `g2sz.67`, `g2sz.68`, `ihgy.38`.

## Out of scope for this issue

Mechanical fixes from the same review (nullable fields, `DatafeedEsqlGates` validate pattern, REST capability caching, transport version bump, etc.) are addressed on the PR branch.

- Parent PR: #160856
- Stack split: [#160857](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/160857)+ (parts 2–4); review fixes on `ml-esql-datafeeds-part2` (`fbb7d8fc5a36`), restacked part3/part4.

issue.title: [ML] ES|QL datafeeds: shrink a truncated chunk and record the incomplete interval

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
## Summary

When an ES|QL chunk hits the injected row limit, `ChunkedDataExtractor` shrinks the chunk and retries (up to six attempts) instead of silently dropping rows past the limit. If still truncated, it records the interval via `getIncompleteSearchInterval()`.

- Row-limit injection is decided once (`EsqlDataExtractor.injectsRowLimit` → `injectsEsqlRowLimit` on the chunked context).
- After a successful shrink, the learned chunk span is carried forward; sparse complete chunks regrow span toward `DEFAULT_ESQL_CHUNK_DOCS / rowCount` (capped at the initial estimate) only when the chunk did not need shrinking (no regrow right after a shrink retry).
- Shrink, regrow, truncation-decision, and incomplete-interval logic live in `ChunkedDataExtractorEsqlSizing` with unit tests. A truncated result always has exactly the injected row limit, so a shrink scales the chunk by a constant 1/2 (aligned down to the grouping interval, minimum one interval).
- `getIncompleteSearchInterval()` returns the span from the earliest truncated chunk start to the latest truncated chunk end (complete chunks in between may lie inside that span).
- `cancel()` sets the flag before cancelling the delegate; `installExtractor` re-checks after swap.
- Known limits: a user `LIMIT` at exactly the injected cap, or above the server cap, is not treated as truncation; lowering `esql.query.result_truncation_max_size` below the injected cap defeats truncation detection.

Producer for #163845 (audit) and #163851 (delayed-data detector).

labels.name: repo-51e13d60

issue.body:
ES|QL datafeeds had no delayed-data detection. `EsqlDelayedDataDetector` re-queries the finalized buckets and compares the counts with what the datafeed processed. `DelayedDataDetectorFactory.buildDetector` takes the `DataExtractorFactory` and picks it for ES|QL datafeeds; the DSL path is unchanged.

- Summary counts are read the way autodetect reads them: any value goes through a double, negatives and values that round to zero are ignored, and the rest is rounded half up. Bare hex strings are not supported.
- `DelayedDataDetector` gets a default `cancel()`. `DatafeedJob.cancelActiveExtractor()` calls it, so stop and isolate abort an in-flight re-query, and the job re-checks running and isolated state before writing an annotation.
- A truncated re-query is logged at DEBUG.

 Must merge after the B2 slice (#164119) (it needs `getIncompleteSearchInterval()` to be populated), and before the slice that routes `esql_query` datafeeds in `DataExtractorFactory` (B1), so delayed-data checks cannot hit a null detector.

issue.title: Meter find_structure memory against indices.breaker.request

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #158927. That PR bounds concurrent `find_structure` analyses to `EsExecutors.allocatedProcessors(settings)` and removes per-value `Pattern.compile` from the mapping-guess hot path, but two memory limits remain open.

## Gaps left by #158927

### 1. Unbounded throttle queue

`ThrottledTaskRunner` uses a `LinkedTransferQueue`, i.e. an unbounded queue. `RestController` holds each request body against the in-flight breaker until the *response* completes, so a large enough burst of concurrent requests still accumulates request bodies in heap (e.g. ~200 queued requests × ~2.8 MB body ≈ ~560 MB on top of in-flight analyses).

### 2. Unbounded single-request sample size

`AbstractFindStructureRequest.validate()` places no upper limit on `lines_to_sample`. A single wide, deep sample can still OOM a small node on its own, independent of concurrency.

## Proposed fix

Meter the parse against `indices.breaker.request` so excess or oversized requests receive a 429 instead of risking node OOM. Consider:

- Rejecting or queue-limiting when estimated working-set would exceed breaker budget
- Capping `lines_to_sample` (or total sample bytes) with a sensible default and cluster setting

## Related

- #158927 — concurrency bound (merged/pending)

issue.title: [ML] Nightly maintenance should delete emptied rolled .ml-anomalies-* results indices

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
## Description

Nightly ML maintenance rolls `.ml-anomalies-*` indices at `xpack.ml.results_index_rollover_max_size` (#131014, #136065), but nothing removes a rolled results index once retention has emptied it. This is a design gap: the state indices already have the cleanup (`EmptyStateIndexRemover`), the results indices do not. The nightly maintenance should delete emptied rolled results indices.

### Current behaviour (checked at `v9.4.7` and `main`)

- `ExpiredResultsRemover` runs one delete-by-query per job through the job's read alias. It never drops an index.
- `EmptyStateIndexRemover` deletes empty `.ml-state*` indices that are not behind the write alias. It is wired into `TransportDeleteExpiredDataAction`. No equivalent exists for `.ml-anomalies-*`.
- `JobDataDeleter` drops a results index only on job delete, and only if no other job's documents remain in it.
- After each roll, `MlIndexAndAlias.addResultsIndexRolloverAliasActions` re-adds every job's filtered read alias to the new index, from the earliest index that had it (`addReadAliasesForResultsIndices`). A job's read alias therefore spans every backing index.

### Impact

With `results_retention_days` set, old backing indices end up with no retained results documents. The retention delete excludes `model_size_stats`, `forecast` and `forecast_request_stats`, so those can remain. The indices stay in the cluster, keep their shards, and keep one read-alias entry per job, forever.

Example: a shared custom index for ~1,700 jobs at ~8.6 GB/day rolls about every 6 days. That is ~60 backing indices a year, each carrying ~1,700 read-alias entries (~100k alias entries a year), and every job's read alias searches all of them.

### Proposed fix

Add a results-index counterpart to `EmptyStateIndexRemover` to the delete-expired-data step of the nightly maintenance. It deletes a rolled results index when:

- it is not the latest index of its family (no job's write alias points at it), and
- it holds no documents that retention keeps.

Points to settle in the implementation:

- Treatment of `model_size_stats` and forecast documents in an otherwise empty index. A job that stopped writing before the roll must keep its latest `model_size_stats`.
- A stopped job's results are never expired, because the retention cutoff is relative to the job's latest bucket. Its index is not empty and is kept, which is correct.
- Respect indices with an ILM policy, as the rollover does (`hasIlm`).
- Naming is safe: `MlIndexAndAlias.nextSuffix` uses the highest existing suffix + 1, so deleting old indices does not cause reuse.

issue.title: [ML] A job awaiting node assignment is silent in logs: findLongTimeUnassignedTasks skips tasks with null state

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
## Mechanism (read at upstream/main d99fc204)

`findLongTimeUnassignedTasks`:

    if (task.getExecutorNode() == null) {
        if (JOB_TASK_NAME or DATA_FRAME_ANALYTICS_TASK_NAME) {
            // Ignore failed tasks - they don't need to be assigned to a node
            if (task.getState() == null || ((MlTaskState) task.getState()).isFailed()) { continue; }

The comment justifies skipping failed tasks, but the condition also skips `state == null`. An open-job persistent task that has never been assigned has no state yet (state is set by the executor node), so a job that is never assigned is exactly the null-state case and is never reported by the "ML persistent tasks unassigned for a long time" WARN. Per-node rejection reasons live in `JobNodeSelector` at trace level and in the task's `Assignment.getExplanation()`, which is only logged by the audit path when `alwaysAuditUnassigned`/explanation changes and, for jobs, goes to the job audit (notifications index) rather than the server log.

Proof level: code read of the skip condition (certain); that a never-assigned job has null state is inferred from the persistent-task model and not executed here. Needs one QA repro: open a job with no eligible node and check the notifier output over time.

issue.body:

issue.title: [ML] `JobResultsPersister.Builder` keeps a permanently rejected document queued and resubmits it with every later bulk

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
Tested commit: `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25` (`upstream/main`, 2026-11-04).

A document that the results index permanently rejects (HTTP 400, for example a
keyword value longer than Lucene's 32766 byte term limit) stays in the pending
item map of `JobResultsPersister.Builder`. Every later `executeRequest()` sends
that document again, together with all newer results, and fails again with the
same `IrrecoverableException`. The queue only empties when the job's
`AutodetectResultProcessor` is discarded (job close, node vacate, process
restart).

The sighting that led here was observed in a serverless production project,
details masked: the same few result document ids were re-sent on every flush,
and every flush acknowledgement failed for days until the job was restarted.
This issue does not claim that this was the cause in that project; it describes
what the code does when a document is rejected.

## Mechanism

1. `JobResultsPersister.Builder.executeRequest()` clears its queue only after
   `bulkIndexWithRetry` returns normally ([JobResultsPersister.java L289-L304](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/persistence/JobResultsPersister.java#L289-L304)).
   If it throws, `items` is untouched.
2. `ResultsPersisterService` inspects bulk responses item by item. The first
   item whose failure is classified irrecoverable fails the whole call with an
   `IrrecoverableException`, with no retry ([ResultsPersisterService.java L359-L384](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/persistence/ResultsPersisterService.java#L359-L384)).
   `BAD_REQUEST` is in the irrecoverable status set ([MlRecoverableErrorClassifier.java L50-L59](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/MlRecoverableErrorClassifier.java#L50-L59)).
   The other items of that bulk were already processed by the index and are
   not at fault.
3. The exception does not discard the builder. `AutodetectResultProcessor.readResults()`
   catches every exception per result and continues while the process is
   alive ([AutodetectResultProcessor.java L211-L228](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/output/AutodetectResultProcessor.java#L211-L228),
   `isAlive()` at [L593-L598](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/output/AutodetectResultProcessor.java#L593-L598)).
   The `bulkResultsPersister` field is `final`, so the same builder instance,
   with the same queued document, serves the next result.
4. Consequences in the same path: the rest of `processResult` for the failing
   result is skipped (records, influencers, ... after the bucket), `deleteInterimRequired`
   is not updated, and a failing flush acknowledgement is reported to the
   waiting flush call as an error each time.

Also relevant, but separate from the claim above: when the failure is classified
recoverable the same call can block the results thread for the full retry
schedule (default `xpack.ml.persist_results_max_retries` = 20, exponential backoff
capped at 15 minutes, `currentAttempt > maxFailureRetries` at
[L499](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/persistence/ResultsPersisterService.java#L499)),
and when it gives up it throws a `RecoverableException` without cause, so the
item failure class is not visible in the exception. That part is not addressed
by the proposed change.

## What can carry an over-long value (code facts only)

`.ml-anomalies-*` mappings ([results_index_mappings.json](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/ml/anomalydetection/results_index_mappings.json)):
`by_field_value`, `over_field_value`, `partition_field_value`,
`correlated_by_field_value` (top level and under `causes`), `influencer_field_value`,
`influencer_field_values`, `regex` are plain `keyword` fields with no
`ignore_above`. The dynamic template maps any other non-object field to `keyword`
as well. The `*_field_value` fields additionally `copy_to` the `whitespace`-analysed
text field `all_field_values`. `KeywordFieldMapper` rejects a value longer than
the Lucene maximum term length before indexing ([KeywordFieldMapper.java L2428-L2438](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/KeywordFieldMapper.java#L2428-L2438)),
with `IllegalArgumentException: Document contains at least one immense term in field=...`,
which surfaces as a 400 bulk item failure. Nothing on the Java side of the results
persistence path bounds the length of these values.

## Reproduction (unit test, fails on `a013f1d20e15`)

`JobResultsPersisterTests#testExecuteRequest_PermanentlyRejectedItemIsNotResubmitted`:
a mocked client answers every bulk item by item and fails one bucket document
with a `DocumentParsingException` (cause: immense term `IllegalArgumentException`).
The test calls `executeRequest()` twice with a newer bucket added in between.

```
java.lang.AssertionError: permanently rejected document is not resubmitted
    Expected: not a collection containing "foo_bucket_1000000_600"
         but: was <[foo_bucket_1000000_600, foo_bucket_2000000_600]>
    at ...JobResultsPersisterTests.testExecuteRequest_PermanentlyRejectedItemIsNotResubmitted(JobResultsPersisterTests.java:327)
1 test completed, 1 failed
```

The second bulk contains the rejected document again next to the newer one.

## Observed vs expected

- Observed: a permanently rejected document is part of every following bulk and
  makes every following `executeRequest()` throw.
- Expected: the rejected document is dropped after the first rejection (it can
  never be indexed), newer results are persisted normally, the failure is
  still reported once.

## Fix direction

Proposed (small, kept narrow on purpose): `IrrecoverableException` carries the
ids of items rejected as invalid documents (irrecoverable and status 400);
`Builder.executeRequest()` removes exactly those ids from its queue before
rethrowing. Everything else is unchanged:

| Failure | Behaviour after change |
|---|---|
| transient item failure | unchanged: items retried, queue kept when retries run out |
| permanent 400 item | item dropped from queue, exception still thrown once |
| permanent non-400 item (e.g. 404 missing index) | unchanged: queue kept, a later call can deliver once the cause is resolved |
| whole-bulk failure, shutdown, reset mode | unchanged |

Further options, not part of the change above: cap or `ignore_above` the
affected keyword fields; chain the first item failure into `RecoverableException`
so the failure class is logged when retries are exhausted.

A fix with the test follows in a PR.

## Related

No duplicate found (searches in `elastic/elasticsearch` for `JobResultsPersister`,
`ResultsPersisterService`, `bulkIndexWithRetry`, `immense term`, `IrrecoverableException`,
`by_field_value`, `ignore_above anomaly results`). Open PR #164451 touches the
retry WARN level in `ResultsPersisterService` and may need a trivial merge with this change.

issue.body:
## Summary

`POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/<job>/_update` with a detector update that has only `detector_index` and `description` (no `custom_rules`) on an **open** job returns `200`, and the config change is saved. The update that should be pushed to the running autodetect process fails with a `NullPointerException` and is only logged. Anything else sent in the same request that the process needs to know about (`model_plot_config`, `per_partition_categorization`, `groups` -> scheduled events, rules on another detector) is dropped from the running process until the job is reopened.

The same defect exists in every branch I checked (7.17, 8.0, 8.10, 8.19, 9.2, 9.3, main).

Observed in a serverless production project (stack trace masked).

## Affected versions

- Reproduced at `elastic/elasticsearch` main `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25` (2026-11-04).
- The unguarded `getRules().forEach` is also present on 7.17, 8.0, 8.10, 8.19, 9.2 and 9.3 (checked by reading `UpdateParams.java` on each branch; not reproduced there).

## Reproduction

Needs an open anomaly detection job. `custom_rules` is intentionally not sent.

```
PUT _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro
{
  "analysis_config": { "bucket_span": "15m", "detectors": [ { "function": "count" } ] },
  "data_description": { "time_field": "@timestamp" }
}
POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro/_open

POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro/_update
{
  "model_plot_config": { "enabled": true },
  "detectors": [ { "detector_index": 0, "description": "new description" } ]
}
```

## Observed

- HTTP 200 with the updated job config (description and `model_plot_config` are persisted).
- On the master node (log excerpt from an internalClusterTest run, trimmed):

```
[ERROR][o.e.x.m.j.UpdateJobProcessNotifier] Failed to update remote job [npe-repro]
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.util.List.forEach(java.util.function.Consumer)" because the return value of "...JobUpdate$DetectorUpdate.getRules()" is null
    at ...UpdateParams.lambda$extractReferencedFilters$1(UpdateParams.java:93)
    at ...UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters(UpdateParams.java:92)
    at ...AutodetectProcessManager.writeUpdateProcessMessage(AutodetectProcessManager.java:435)
    at ...TransportUpdateProcessAction.taskOperation(TransportUpdateProcessAction.java:59)
[ERROR][o.e.x.m.j.JobManager] [npe-repro] Updating autodetect failed with an exception, job update [{"job_id":"npe-repro","detectors":[{"detector_index":0,"description":"new description"}], ...
```

- Calling the internal `UpdateProcessAction` directly with the same payload surfaces the NPE to the caller as an `ElasticsearchStatusException` with the NPE message.

A detector update without rules means "leave rules unchanged" (this is how `JobUpdate.mergeWithJob`, `JobUpdate.updatesDetectors`, `AutodetectCommunicator.writeUpdateProcessMessage` and the stream serialization already treat `null`). `extractReferencedFilters()` should skip it, the update should reach the process, and no error should be logged.

- Missing guard: [`UpdateParams.java:93`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/UpdateParams.java#L93) (`detectorUpdate.getRules().forEach(...)`).

- Call chain on an open job: `JobManager.postJobUpdate` (`JobManager.java:440`, `UpdateParams.fromJobUpdate`; only when `JobUpdate.isAutodetectProcessUpdate()` is true, which a non-null `detectorUpdates` always satisfies) -> `UpdateJobProcessNotifier` -> `UpdateProcessAction` -> `TransportUpdateProcessAction.taskOperation` (`:59`) -> `AutodetectProcessManager.writeUpdateProcessMessage` (`:435`) -> `UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters`.

## Proposed fix

Guard `null` in `UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters` (not defaulting rules to an empty list at parse time, because an empty list means "clear all rules" and would change behaviour):

```java
for (JobUpdate.DetectorUpdate detectorUpdate : detectorUpdates) {
    if (detectorUpdate.getRules() != null) {
        detectorUpdate.getRules().forEach(rule -> filterIds.addAll(rule.extractReferencedFilters()));
    }
}
```

- `UpdateParamsTests.testExtractReferencedFilters_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `AutodetectProcessManagerTests.testWriteUpdateProcessMessage_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `UpdateOpenJobDetectorIT.testUpdateProcessAction_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `UpdateOpenJobDetectorIT.testUpdateJob_givenDetectorDescriptionOnlyOnOpenJob` (full `UpdateJobAction` path on an open job)
- `JobUpdateTests.testParse_givenDetectorWithOnlyIndexAndDescription` documents that the REST body yields null rules (passes before and after).

## Not established

- Whether Kibana's job edit flow sends description-only detector updates (if it always sends `custom_rules`, the UI would not hit this).
- Behaviour with the native autodetect process: the IT uses the black-hole process; the failure happens before the process is touched, so the process type should not matter, but it was not run against a native process.

issue.title: [ML] When failing a job open fails, the associated datafeed is force-stopped and stays stopped after the job reopens

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
Observed in a serverless production project during a regional master-election outage (details masked). Not investigated further and not reproduced.

After the open retry budget (`xpack.ml.job_open_retry_timeout`, default 60 min) is exhausted, `OpenJobPersistentTasksExecutor.failTask` tries to commit the FAILED job state. When that state update also fails, the code logs ERROR, calls `jobTask.markAsFailed(e)` and still runs `stopAssociatedDatafeedForFailedJob`, which force-stops the datafeed (read at the serverless build of the time, `OpenJobPersistentTasksExecutor.java` lines 447-465 and 488).

What was observed afterwards: 23 jobs were reopened after recovery but only 7 datafeeds were started again; the rest stayed stopped, and the daily maintenance auto-closed the idle jobs one to two days later.

Not established: the committed job state at that time, whether stopping the datafeed on a failed job is the intended design, and a reproduction (stop the index tier for longer than the retry timeout, then recover).

`findLongTimeUnassignedTasks`:

    if (task.getExecutorNode() == null) {
        if (JOB_TASK_NAME or DATA_FRAME_ANALYTICS_TASK_NAME) {

issue.title: [ML] `JobResultsPersister.Builder` keeps a permanently rejected document queued and resubmits it with every later bulk

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
Tested commit: `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25` (`upstream/main`, 2026-11-04).

A document that the results index permanently rejects (HTTP 400, for example a
keyword value longer than Lucene's 32766 byte term limit) stays in the pending
item map of `JobResultsPersister.Builder`. Every later `executeRequest()` sends
that document again, together with all newer results, and fails again with the
same `IrrecoverableException`. The queue only empties when the job's
`AutodetectResultProcessor` is discarded (job close, node vacate, process
restart).

The sighting that led here was observed in a serverless production project,
details masked: the same few result document ids were re-sent on every flush,
and every flush acknowledgement failed for days until the job was restarted.
This issue does not claim that this was the cause in that project; it describes
what the code does when a document is rejected.

## Mechanism

1. `JobResultsPersister.Builder.executeRequest()` clears its queue only after
   `bulkIndexWithRetry` returns normally ([JobResultsPersister.java L289-L304](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/persistence/JobResultsPersister.java#L289-L304)).
   If it throws, `items` is untouched.
2. `ResultsPersisterService` inspects bulk responses item by item. The first
   item whose failure is classified irrecoverable fails the whole call with an
   `IrrecoverableException`, with no retry ([ResultsPersisterService.java L359-L384](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/persistence/ResultsPersisterService.java#L359-L384)).
   `BAD_REQUEST` is in the irrecoverable status set ([MlRecoverableErrorClassifier.java L50-L59](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/MlRecoverableErrorClassifier.java#L50-L59)).
   The other items of that bulk were already processed by the index and are
   not at fault.
3. The exception does not discard the builder. `AutodetectResultProcessor.readResults()`
   catches every exception per result and continues while the process is
   alive ([AutodetectResultProcessor.java L211-L228](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/output/AutodetectResultProcessor.java#L211-L228),
   `isAlive()` at [L593-L598](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/output/AutodetectResultProcessor.java#L593-L598)).
   The `bulkResultsPersister` field is `final`, so the same builder instance,
   with the same queued document, serves the next result.
4. Consequences in the same path: the rest of `processResult` for the failing
   result is skipped (records, influencers, ... after the bucket), `deleteInterimRequired`
   is not updated, and a failing flush acknowledgement is reported to the
   waiting flush call as an error each time.

Also relevant, but separate from the claim above: when the failure is classified
recoverable the same call can block the results thread for the full retry
schedule (default `xpack.ml.persist_results_max_retries` = 20, exponential backoff
capped at 15 minutes, `currentAttempt > maxFailureRetries` at
[L499](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/persistence/ResultsPersisterService.java#L499)),
and when it gives up it throws a `RecoverableException` without cause, so the
item failure class is not visible in the exception. That part is not addressed
by the proposed change.

## What can carry an over-long value (code facts only)

`.ml-anomalies-*` mappings ([results_index_mappings.json](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/ml/anomalydetection/results_index_mappings.json)):
`by_field_value`, `over_field_value`, `partition_field_value`,
`correlated_by_field_value` (top level and under `causes`), `influencer_field_value`,
`influencer_field_values`, `regex` are plain `keyword` fields with no
`ignore_above`. The dynamic template maps any other non-object field to `keyword`
as well. The `*_field_value` fields additionally `copy_to` the `whitespace`-analysed
text field `all_field_values`. `KeywordFieldMapper` rejects a value longer than
the Lucene maximum term length before indexing ([KeywordFieldMapper.java L2428-L2438](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/KeywordFieldMapper.java#L2428-L2438)),
with `IllegalArgumentException: Document contains at least one immense term in field=...`,
which surfaces as a 400 bulk item failure. Nothing on the Java side of the results
persistence path bounds the length of these values.

## Reproduction (unit test, fails on `a013f1d20e15`)

`JobResultsPersisterTests#testExecuteRequest_PermanentlyRejectedItemIsNotResubmitted`:
a mocked client answers every bulk item by item and fails one bucket document
with a `DocumentParsingException` (cause: immense term `IllegalArgumentException`).
The test calls `executeRequest()` twice with a newer bucket added in between.

```
java.lang.AssertionError: permanently rejected document is not resubmitted
    Expected: not a collection containing "foo_bucket_1000000_600"
         but: was <[foo_bucket_1000000_600, foo_bucket_2000000_600]>
    at ...JobResultsPersisterTests.testExecuteRequest_PermanentlyRejectedItemIsNotResubmitted(JobResultsPersisterTests.java:327)
1 test completed, 1 failed
```

The second bulk contains the rejected document again next to the newer one.

## Observed vs expected

- Observed: a permanently rejected document is part of every following bulk and
  makes every following `executeRequest()` throw.
- Expected: the rejected document is dropped after the first rejection (it can
  never be indexed), newer results are persisted normally, the failure is
  still reported once.

## Fix direction

Proposed (small, kept narrow on purpose): `IrrecoverableException` carries the
ids of items rejected as invalid documents (irrecoverable and status 400);
`Builder.executeRequest()` removes exactly those ids from its queue before
rethrowing. Everything else is unchanged:

| Failure | Behaviour after change |
|---|---|
| transient item failure | unchanged: items retried, queue kept when retries run out |
| permanent 400 item | item dropped from queue, exception still thrown once |
| permanent non-400 item (e.g. 404 missing index) | unchanged: queue kept, a later call can deliver once the cause is resolved |
| whole-bulk failure, shutdown, reset mode | unchanged |

Further options, not part of the change above: cap or `ignore_above` the
affected keyword fields; chain the first item failure into `RecoverableException`
so the failure class is logged when retries are exhausted.

A fix with the test follows in a PR.

## Related

No duplicate found (searches in `elastic/elasticsearch` for `JobResultsPersister`,
`ResultsPersisterService`, `bulkIndexWithRetry`, `immense term`, `IrrecoverableException`,
`by_field_value`, `ignore_above anomaly results`). Open PR #164451 touches the
retry WARN level in `ResultsPersisterService` and may need a trivial merge with this change.

In `ResultsPersisterService.BulkRetryableAction` (upstream/main d99fc204), a failed bulk item is logged only when `isIrrecoverable(cause)` is true. For every item failure classified as recoverable, the code rewrites the request and signals `new RecoverableException()`, which has no message and no cause. From there:

- `MlRetryableAction.calculateDelayBound` logs WARN "failed to index after [N] attempts. Will attempt again." with no reason;

issue.title: [ML] `JobResultsPersister.Builder` keeps a permanently rejected document queued and resubmits it with every later bulk

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
Tested commit: `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25` (`upstream/main`, 2026-11-04).

A document that the results index permanently rejects (HTTP 400, for example a
keyword value longer than Lucene's 32766 byte term limit) stays in the pending
item map of `JobResultsPersister.Builder`. Every later `executeRequest()` sends
that document again, together with all newer results, and fails again with the
same `IrrecoverableException`. The queue only empties when the job's
`AutodetectResultProcessor` is discarded (job close, node vacate, process
restart).

The sighting that led here was observed in a serverless production project,
details masked: the same few result document ids were re-sent on every flush,
and every flush acknowledgement failed for days until the job was restarted.
This issue does not claim that this was the cause in that project; it describes
what the code does when a document is rejected.

## Mechanism

1. `JobResultsPersister.Builder.executeRequest()` clears its queue only after
   `bulkIndexWithRetry` returns normally ([JobResultsPersister.java L289-L304](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/persistence/JobResultsPersister.java#L289-L304)).
   If it throws, `items` is untouched.
2. `ResultsPersisterService` inspects bulk responses item by item. The first
   item whose failure is classified irrecoverable fails the whole call with an
   `IrrecoverableException`, with no retry ([ResultsPersisterService.java L359-L384](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/persistence/ResultsPersisterService.java#L359-L384)).
   `BAD_REQUEST` is in the irrecoverable status set ([MlRecoverableErrorClassifier.java L50-L59](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/MlRecoverableErrorClassifier.java#L50-L59)).
   The other items of that bulk were already processed by the index and are
   not at fault.
3. The exception does not discard the builder. `AutodetectResultProcessor.readResults()`
   catches every exception per result and continues while the process is
   alive ([AutodetectResultProcessor.java L211-L228](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/output/AutodetectResultProcessor.java#L211-L228),
   `isAlive()` at [L593-L598](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/output/AutodetectResultProcessor.java#L593-L598)).
   The `bulkResultsPersister` field is `final`, so the same builder instance,
   with the same queued document, serves the next result.
4. Consequences in the same path: the rest of `processResult` for the failing
   result is skipped (records, influencers, ... after the bucket), `deleteInterimRequired`
   is not updated, and a failing flush acknowledgement is reported to the
   waiting flush call as an error each time.

Also relevant, but separate from the claim above: when the failure is classified
recoverable the same call can block the results thread for the full retry
schedule (default `xpack.ml.persist_results_max_retries` = 20, exponential backoff
capped at 15 minutes, `currentAttempt > maxFailureRetries` at
[L499](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/persistence/ResultsPersisterService.java#L499)),
and when it gives up it throws a `RecoverableException` without cause, so the
item failure class is not visible in the exception. That part is not addressed
by the proposed change.

## What can carry an over-long value (code facts only)

`.ml-anomalies-*` mappings ([results_index_mappings.json](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/ml/anomalydetection/results_index_mappings.json)):
`by_field_value`, `over_field_value`, `partition_field_value`,
`correlated_by_field_value` (top level and under `causes`), `influencer_field_value`,
`influencer_field_values`, `regex` are plain `keyword` fields with no
`ignore_above`. The dynamic template maps any other non-object field to `keyword`
as well. The `*_field_value` fields additionally `copy_to` the `whitespace`-analysed
text field `all_field_values`. `KeywordFieldMapper` rejects a value longer than
the Lucene maximum term length before indexing ([KeywordFieldMapper.java L2428-L2438](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/KeywordFieldMapper.java#L2428-L2438)),
with `IllegalArgumentException: Document contains at least one immense term in field=...`,
which surfaces as a 400 bulk item failure. Nothing on the Java side of the results
persistence path bounds the length of these values.

## Reproduction (unit test, fails on `a013f1d20e15`)

`JobResultsPersisterTests#testExecuteRequest_PermanentlyRejectedItemIsNotResubmitted`:
a mocked client answers every bulk item by item and fails one bucket document
with a `DocumentParsingException` (cause: immense term `IllegalArgumentException`).
The test calls `executeRequest()` twice with a newer bucket added in between.

```
java.lang.AssertionError: permanently rejected document is not resubmitted
    Expected: not a collection containing "foo_bucket_1000000_600"
         but: was <[foo_bucket_1000000_600, foo_bucket_2000000_600]>
    at ...JobResultsPersisterTests.testExecuteRequest_PermanentlyRejectedItemIsNotResubmitted(JobResultsPersisterTests.java:327)
1 test completed, 1 failed
```

The second bulk contains the rejected document again next to the newer one.

## Observed vs expected

- Observed: a permanently rejected document is part of every following bulk and
  makes every following `executeRequest()` throw.
- Expected: the rejected document is dropped after the first rejection (it can
  never be indexed), newer results are persisted normally, the failure is
  still reported once.

## Fix direction

Proposed (small, kept narrow on purpose): `IrrecoverableException` carries the
ids of items rejected as invalid documents (irrecoverable and status 400);
`Builder.executeRequest()` removes exactly those ids from its queue before
rethrowing. Everything else is unchanged:

| Failure | Behaviour after change |
|---|---|
| transient item failure | unchanged: items retried, queue kept when retries run out |
| permanent 400 item | item dropped from queue, exception still thrown once |
| permanent non-400 item (e.g. 404 missing index) | unchanged: queue kept, a later call can deliver once the cause is resolved |
| whole-bulk failure, shutdown, reset mode | unchanged |

Further options, not part of the change above: cap or `ignore_above` the
affected keyword fields; chain the first item failure into `RecoverableException`
so the failure class is logged when retries are exhausted.

A fix with the test follows in a PR.

## Related

No duplicate found (searches in `elastic/elasticsearch` for `JobResultsPersister`,
`ResultsPersisterService`, `bulkIndexWithRetry`, `immense term`, `IrrecoverableException`,
`by_field_value`, `ignore_above anomaly results`). Open PR #164451 touches the
retry WARN level in `ResultsPersisterService` and may need a trivial merge with this change.

The update that should be pushed to the running autodetect process fails with a `NullPointerException` and is only logged. Anything else sent in the same request that the process needs to know about (`model_plot_config`, `per_partition_categorization`, `groups` -> scheduled events, rules on another detector) is dropped from the running process until the job is reopened.

The same defect exists in every branch I checked (7.17, 8.0, 8.10, 8.19, 9.2, 9.3, main).

Observed in a serverless production project (stack trace masked).

## Affected versions

- Reproduced at `elastic/elasticsearch` main `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25` (2026-11-04).
- The unguarded `getRules().forEach` is also present on 7.17, 8.0, 8.10, 8.19, 9.2 and 9.3 (checked by reading `UpdateParams.java` on each branch; not reproduced there).

## Reproduction

Needs an open anomaly detection job. `custom_rules` is intentionally not sent.

```
PUT _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro
{
  "analysis_config": { "bucket_span": "15m", "detectors": [ { "function": "count" } ] },
  "data_description": { "time_field": "@timestamp" }
}
POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro/_open

POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro/_update
{
  "model_plot_config": { "enabled": true },
  "detectors": [ { "detector_index": 0, "description": "new description" } ]
}
```

## Observed

- HTTP 200 with the updated job config (description and `model_plot_config` are persisted).
- On the master node (log excerpt from an internalClusterTest run, trimmed):

```
[ERROR][o.e.x.m.j.UpdateJobProcessNotifier] Failed to update remote job [npe-repro]
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.util.List.forEach(java.util.function.Consumer)" because the return value of "...JobUpdate$DetectorUpdate.getRules()" is null
    at ...UpdateParams.lambda$extractReferencedFilters$1(UpdateParams.java:93)
    at ...UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters(UpdateParams.java:92)
    at ...AutodetectProcessManager.writeUpdateProcessMessage(AutodetectProcessManager.java:435)
    at ...TransportUpdateProcessAction.taskOperation(TransportUpdateProcessAction.java:59)
[ERROR][o.e.x.m.j.JobManager] [npe-repro] Updating autodetect failed with an exception, job update [{"job_id":"npe-repro","detectors":[{"detector_index":0,"description":"new description"}], ...
```

- Calling the internal `UpdateProcessAction` directly with the same payload surfaces the NPE to the caller as an `ElasticsearchStatusException` with the NPE message.
- The process never receives the `model_plot_config` change. `extractReferencedFilters()` runs at the top of `writeUpdateProcessMessage`, before anything is written, so the whole message is lost.

## Expected

A detector update without rules means "leave rules unchanged" (this is how `JobUpdate.mergeWithJob`, `JobUpdate.updatesDetectors`, `AutodetectCommunicator.writeUpdateProcessMessage` and the stream serialization already treat `null`). `extractReferencedFilters()` should skip it, the update should reach the process, and no error should be logged.

## Root cause / code pointers (all at `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25`)

- Missing guard: [`UpdateParams.java:93`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/UpdateParams.java#L93) (`detectorUpdate.getRules().forEach(...)`).
- `null` rules are valid and produced by the REST parser: [`JobUpdate.DetectorUpdate.PARSER`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/ml/job/config/JobUpdate.java#L664-L677) declares `custom_rules` with `optionalConstructorArg()`; the wire constructor also yields `null` when the boolean flag is false.
- Call chain on an open job: `JobManager.postJobUpdate` (`JobManager.java:440`, `UpdateParams.fromJobUpdate`; only when `JobUpdate.isAutodetectProcessUpdate()` is true, which a non-null `detectorUpdates` always satisfies) -> `UpdateJobProcessNotifier` -> `UpdateProcessAction` -> `TransportUpdateProcessAction.taskOperation` (`:59`) -> `AutodetectProcessManager.writeUpdateProcessMessage` (`:435`) -> `UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters`.
- Why the client sees success: `JobManager.postJobUpdate` returns `PutJobAction.Response` at `JobManager.java:462` regardless of the process-update outcome; the failure is only logged (`JobManager.java:449`, `UpdateJobProcessNotifier.java:168`).
- Neighbouring code that already handles `null` rules: `JobUpdate.java:482` (`mergeWithJob`) and `AutodetectCommunicator.java:~242`.

## Proposed fix

Guard `null` in `UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters` (not defaulting rules to an empty list at parse time, because an empty list means "clear all rules" and would change behaviour):

```java
for (JobUpdate.DetectorUpdate detectorUpdate : detectorUpdates) {
    if (detectorUpdate.getRules() != null) {
        detectorUpdate.getRules().forEach(rule -> filterIds.addAll(rule.extractReferencedFilters()));
    }
}
```

A fix with tests follows in a PR. The tests below fail before the fix and pass after:

- `UpdateParamsTests.testExtractReferencedFilters_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `AutodetectProcessManagerTests.testWriteUpdateProcessMessage_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `UpdateOpenJobDetectorIT.testUpdateProcessAction_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `UpdateOpenJobDetectorIT.testUpdateJob_givenDetectorDescriptionOnlyOnOpenJob` (full `UpdateJobAction` path on an open job)
- `JobUpdateTests.testParse_givenDetectorWithOnlyIndexAndDescription` documents that the REST body yields null rules (passes before and after).

## Not established

- Whether Kibana's job edit flow sends description-only detector updates (if it always sends `custom_rules`, the UI would not hit this).
- Behaviour with the native autodetect process: the IT uses the black-hole process; the failure happens before the process is touched, so the process type should not matter, but it was not run against a native process.

issue.title: [ML] `JobResultsPersister.Builder` keeps a permanently rejected document queued and resubmits it with every later bulk

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
Tested commit: `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25` (`upstream/main`, 2026-11-04).

A document that the results index permanently rejects (HTTP 400, for example a
keyword value longer than Lucene's 32766 byte term limit) stays in the pending
item map of `JobResultsPersister.Builder`. Every later `executeRequest()` sends
that document again, together with all newer results, and fails again with the
same `IrrecoverableException`. The queue only empties when the job's
`AutodetectResultProcessor` is discarded (job close, node vacate, process
restart).

The sighting that led here was observed in a serverless production project,
details masked: the same few result document ids were re-sent on every flush,
and every flush acknowledgement failed for days until the job was restarted.
This issue does not claim that this was the cause in that project; it describes
what the code does when a document is rejected.

## Mechanism

1. `JobResultsPersister.Builder.executeRequest()` clears its queue only after
   `bulkIndexWithRetry` returns normally ([JobResultsPersister.java L289-L304](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/persistence/JobResultsPersister.java#L289-L304)).
   If it throws, `items` is untouched.
2. `ResultsPersisterService` inspects bulk responses item by item. The first
   item whose failure is classified irrecoverable fails the whole call with an
   `IrrecoverableException`, with no retry ([ResultsPersisterService.java L359-L384](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/persistence/ResultsPersisterService.java#L359-L384)).
   `BAD_REQUEST` is in the irrecoverable status set ([MlRecoverableErrorClassifier.java L50-L59](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/MlRecoverableErrorClassifier.java#L50-L59)).
   The other items of that bulk were already processed by the index and are
   not at fault.
3. The exception does not discard the builder. `AutodetectResultProcessor.readResults()`
   catches every exception per result and continues while the process is
   alive ([AutodetectResultProcessor.java L211-L228](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/output/AutodetectResultProcessor.java#L211-L228),
   `isAlive()` at [L593-L598](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/output/AutodetectResultProcessor.java#L593-L598)).
   The `bulkResultsPersister` field is `final`, so the same builder instance,
   with the same queued document, serves the next result.
4. Consequences in the same path: the rest of `processResult` for the failing
   result is skipped (records, influencers, ... after the bucket), `deleteInterimRequired`
   is not updated, and a failing flush acknowledgement is reported to the
   waiting flush call as an error each time.

Also relevant, but separate from the claim above: when the failure is classified
recoverable the same call can block the results thread for the full retry
schedule (default `xpack.ml.persist_results_max_retries` = 20, exponential backoff
capped at 15 minutes, `currentAttempt > maxFailureRetries` at
[L499](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/utils/persistence/ResultsPersisterService.java#L499)),
and when it gives up it throws a `RecoverableException` without cause, so the
item failure class is not visible in the exception. That part is not addressed
by the proposed change.

## What can carry an over-long value (code facts only)

`.ml-anomalies-*` mappings ([results_index_mappings.json](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/ml/anomalydetection/results_index_mappings.json)):
`by_field_value`, `over_field_value`, `partition_field_value`,
`correlated_by_field_value` (top level and under `causes`), `influencer_field_value`,
`influencer_field_values`, `regex` are plain `keyword` fields with no
`ignore_above`. The dynamic template maps any other non-object field to `keyword`
as well. The `*_field_value` fields additionally `copy_to` the `whitespace`-analysed
text field `all_field_values`. `KeywordFieldMapper` rejects a value longer than
the Lucene maximum term length before indexing ([KeywordFieldMapper.java L2428-L2438](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/KeywordFieldMapper.java#L2428-L2438)),
with `IllegalArgumentException: Document contains at least one immense term in field=...`,
which surfaces as a 400 bulk item failure. Nothing on the Java side of the results
persistence path bounds the length of these values.

## Reproduction (unit test, fails on `a013f1d20e15`)

`JobResultsPersisterTests#testExecuteRequest_PermanentlyRejectedItemIsNotResubmitted`:
a mocked client answers every bulk item by item and fails one bucket document
with a `DocumentParsingException` (cause: immense term `IllegalArgumentException`).
The test calls `executeRequest()` twice with a newer bucket added in between.

```
java.lang.AssertionError: permanently rejected document is not resubmitted
    Expected: not a collection containing "foo_bucket_1000000_600"
         but: was <[foo_bucket_1000000_600, foo_bucket_2000000_600]>
    at ...JobResultsPersisterTests.testExecuteRequest_PermanentlyRejectedItemIsNotResubmitted(JobResultsPersisterTests.java:327)
1 test completed, 1 failed
```

The second bulk contains the rejected document again next to the newer one.

## Observed vs expected

- Observed: a permanently rejected document is part of every following bulk and
  makes every following `executeRequest()` throw.
- Expected: the rejected document is dropped after the first rejection (it can
  never be indexed), newer results are persisted normally, the failure is
  still reported once.

## Fix direction

Proposed (small, kept narrow on purpose): `IrrecoverableException` carries the
ids of items rejected as invalid documents (irrecoverable and status 400);
`Builder.executeRequest()` removes exactly those ids from its queue before
rethrowing. Everything else is unchanged:

| Failure | Behaviour after change |
|---|---|

issue.title: [ML] Updating a detector's description on an open anomaly detection job throws an NPE in UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters; the running process misses the whole update

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
## Summary

`POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/<job>/_update` with a detector update that has only `detector_index` and `description` (no `custom_rules`) on an **open** job returns `200`, and the config change is saved. The update that should be pushed to the running autodetect process fails with a `NullPointerException` and is only logged. Anything else sent in the same request that the process needs to know about (`model_plot_config`, `per_partition_categorization`, `groups` -> scheduled events, rules on another detector) is dropped from the running process until the job is reopened.

The same defect exists in every branch I checked (7.17, 8.0, 8.10, 8.19, 9.2, 9.3, main).

Observed in a serverless production project (stack trace masked).

## Affected versions

- Reproduced at `elastic/elasticsearch` main `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25` (2026-11-04).
- The unguarded `getRules().forEach` is also present on 7.17, 8.0, 8.10, 8.19, 9.2 and 9.3 (checked by reading `UpdateParams.java` on each branch; not reproduced there).

## Reproduction

Needs an open anomaly detection job. `custom_rules` is intentionally not sent.

```
PUT _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro
{
  "analysis_config": { "bucket_span": "15m", "detectors": [ { "function": "count" } ] },
  "data_description": { "time_field": "@timestamp" }
}
POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro/_open

POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/npe-repro/_update
{
  "model_plot_config": { "enabled": true },
  "detectors": [ { "detector_index": 0, "description": "new description" } ]
}
```

## Observed

- HTTP 200 with the updated job config (description and `model_plot_config` are persisted).
- On the master node (log excerpt from an internalClusterTest run, trimmed):

```
[ERROR][o.e.x.m.j.UpdateJobProcessNotifier] Failed to update remote job [npe-repro]
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.util.List.forEach(java.util.function.Consumer)" because the return value of "...JobUpdate$DetectorUpdate.getRules()" is null
    at ...UpdateParams.lambda$extractReferencedFilters$1(UpdateParams.java:93)
    at ...UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters(UpdateParams.java:92)
    at ...AutodetectProcessManager.writeUpdateProcessMessage(AutodetectProcessManager.java:435)
    at ...TransportUpdateProcessAction.taskOperation(TransportUpdateProcessAction.java:59)
[ERROR][o.e.x.m.j.JobManager] [npe-repro] Updating autodetect failed with an exception, job update [{"job_id":"npe-repro","detectors":[{"detector_index":0,"description":"new description"}], ...
```

- Calling the internal `UpdateProcessAction` directly with the same payload surfaces the NPE to the caller as an `ElasticsearchStatusException` with the NPE message.
- The process never receives the `model_plot_config` change. `extractReferencedFilters()` runs at the top of `writeUpdateProcessMessage`, before anything is written, so the whole message is lost.

## Expected

A detector update without rules means "leave rules unchanged" (this is how `JobUpdate.mergeWithJob`, `JobUpdate.updatesDetectors`, `AutodetectCommunicator.writeUpdateProcessMessage` and the stream serialization already treat `null`). `extractReferencedFilters()` should skip it, the update should reach the process, and no error should be logged.

## Root cause / code pointers (all at `a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25`)

- Missing guard: [`UpdateParams.java:93`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/autodetect/UpdateParams.java#L93) (`detectorUpdate.getRules().forEach(...)`).
- `null` rules are valid and produced by the REST parser: [`JobUpdate.DetectorUpdate.PARSER`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a013f1d20e156e804c383df55b16121cee166e25/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/ml/job/config/JobUpdate.java#L664-L677) declares `custom_rules` with `optionalConstructorArg()`; the wire constructor also yields `null` when the boolean flag is false.
- Call chain on an open job: `JobManager.postJobUpdate` (`JobManager.java:440`, `UpdateParams.fromJobUpdate`; only when `JobUpdate.isAutodetectProcessUpdate()` is true, which a non-null `detectorUpdates` always satisfies) -> `UpdateJobProcessNotifier` -> `UpdateProcessAction` -> `TransportUpdateProcessAction.taskOperation` (`:59`) -> `AutodetectProcessManager.writeUpdateProcessMessage` (`:435`) -> `UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters`.
- Why the client sees success: `JobManager.postJobUpdate` returns `PutJobAction.Response` at `JobManager.java:462` regardless of the process-update outcome; the failure is only logged (`JobManager.java:449`, `UpdateJobProcessNotifier.java:168`).
- Neighbouring code that already handles `null` rules: `JobUpdate.java:482` (`mergeWithJob`) and `AutodetectCommunicator.java:~242`.

## Proposed fix

Guard `null` in `UpdateParams.extractReferencedFilters` (not defaulting rules to an empty list at parse time, because an empty list means "clear all rules" and would change behaviour):

```java
for (JobUpdate.DetectorUpdate detectorUpdate : detectorUpdates) {
    if (detectorUpdate.getRules() != null) {
        detectorUpdate.getRules().forEach(rule -> filterIds.addAll(rule.extractReferencedFilters()));
    }
}
```

A fix with tests follows in a PR. The tests below fail before the fix and pass after:

- `UpdateParamsTests.testExtractReferencedFilters_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `AutodetectProcessManagerTests.testWriteUpdateProcessMessage_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `UpdateOpenJobDetectorIT.testUpdateProcessAction_givenDetectorUpdateWithoutRules`
- `UpdateOpenJobDetectorIT.testUpdateJob_givenDetectorDescriptionOnlyOnOpenJob` (full `UpdateJobAction` path on an open job)
- `JobUpdateTests.testParse_givenDetectorWithOnlyIndexAndDescription` documents that the REST body yields null rules (passes before and after).

## Not established

- Whether Kibana's job edit flow sends description-only detector updates (if it always sends `custom_rules`, the UI would not hit this).
- Behaviour with the native autodetect process: the IT uses the black-hole process; the failure happens before the process is touched, so the process type should not matter, but it was not run against a native process.

issue.title: [ML] Nightly maintenance should delete emptied rolled .ml-anomalies-* results indices

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

issue.body:
## Description

Nightly ML maintenance rolls `.ml-anomalies-*` indices at `xpack.ml.results_index_rollover_max_size` (#131014, #136065), but nothing removes a rolled results index once retention has emptied it. This is a design gap: the state indices already have the cleanup (`EmptyStateIndexRemover`), the results indices do not. The nightly maintenance should delete emptied rolled results indices.

### Current behaviour (checked at `v9.4.7` and `main`)

- `ExpiredResultsRemover` runs one delete-by-query per job through the job's read alias. It never drops an index.
- `EmptyStateIndexRemover` deletes empty `.ml-state*` indices that are not behind the write alias. It is wired into `TransportDeleteExpiredDataAction`. No equivalent exists for `.ml-anomalies-*`.
- `JobDataDeleter` drops a results index only on job delete, and only if no other job's documents remain in it.
- After each roll, `MlIndexAndAlias.addResultsIndexRolloverAliasActions` re-adds every job's filtered read alias to the new index, from the earliest index that had it (`addReadAliasesForResultsIndices`). A job's read alias therefore spans every backing index.

### Impact

With `results_retention_days` set, old backing indices end up with no retained results documents. The retention delete excludes `model_size_stats`, `forecast` and `forecast_request_stats`, so those can remain. The indices stay in the cluster, keep their shards, and keep one read-alias entry per job, forever.

Example: a shared custom index for ~1,700 jobs at ~8.6 GB/day rolls about every 6 days. That is ~60 backing indices a year, each carrying ~1,700 read-alias entries (~100k alias entries a year), and every job's read alias searches all of them.

### Proposed fix

Add a results-index counterpart to `EmptyStateIndexRemover` to the delete-expired-data step of the nightly maintenance. It deletes a rolled results index when:

- it is not the latest index of its family (no job's write alias points at it), and
- it holds no documents that retention keeps.

Points to settle in the implementation:

- Treatment of `model_size_stats` and forecast documents in an otherwise empty index. A job that stopped writing before the roll must keep its latest `model_size_stats`.
- A stopped job's results are never expired, because the retention cutoff is relative to the job's latest bucket. Its index is not empty and is kept, which is correct.
- Respect indices with an ILM policy, as the rollover does (`hasIlm`).
- Naming is safe: `MlIndexAndAlias.nextSuffix` uses the highest existing suffix + 1, so deleting old indices does not cause reuse.
